claim: For the exact zero-order-hold discretization of the continuously controllable planar oscillator \(A=\omega\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}, B=e_1, \omega>0\), the sampled reachability matrix \(W_h=[B_h,A_hB_h]\) is singular exactly at \(h_m=m\pi/\omega\). Its exact singular values imply \(\|W_h^{-1}\|_2\sim1/(\sqrt{2}|h-h_m|)\) at odd resonances and \(\|W_h^{-1}\|_2\sim\sqrt{2}/(\omega|h-h_m|^2)\) at even resonances, so the source's unrestricted sampled-controllability assertion fails and its inverse-based exact-tracking computation becomes ill-conditioned nearby.

limitations: Does not establish a resonance law for arbitrary plants.
Does not quantify the full nonlinear controller's noise response.
Does not address the separate static-feedback theorem under its nilpotent-plant assumption.
Two classical sampled-data controllability papers were available only at abstract level; full-text overlap remains a risk.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.scope: Exact zero-order-hold reachability matrix for a two-dimensional, single-input planar oscillator with fixed positive frequency.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.verification_integrity: Analytic derivation with a standard-library numerical cross-check; no independent audit or external certification is claimed.

title: Critical sampling resonances in a planar oscillator's reachability matrix
